gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-mayan-: Striking up top, Stencilia cuts its curves open and keeps its lines compact. Noto Sans Mayan Numerals handles the body with lowercase that stands lofty and a c that gapes at any size, while the heading simply makes noise.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-meetei: Stencilia leaves generous breaks where its curves end, giving the heading a cut-out, structural look. And Noto Sans Meetei Mayek follows with rounded forms and large lowercase eyes, a cracked-bangle gap that softens the stencil's edge.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-mende-: Structural from the first letter, Stencilia leaves wide breaks at its curve endings. But Noto Sans Mende Kikakui is the real strength here, with daylight through every curve and lowercase that stands up against the capitals.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-meroit: Stencilia is a display face that opens its curve endings wide and squeezes the gap up to its ascenders. And Noto Sans Meroitic lets a long page flow easily, its lowercase filling each line almost like capitals.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-mono: Stencilia gives headings a striking, structural cut, with open curve endings and a compact gap below the ascender line. Noto Sans Mono settles in beneath, letters spaced so nothing bumps.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-mro: Noto Sans Mro gives the text dense, lofty words with big entrances into every letter. Stencilia does best as a striking, structural headline with open curve endings, while Noto Sans Mro does best as a modern body.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-nabata: Stencilia brings a structural, cut-out feel to the headings. Noto Sans Nabataean follows with lowercase rising almost to capital height and wide-open s curves, so the two meet in the middle.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-nag-mu: Contemporary and unfussy, Noto Sans Nag Mundari sits under Stencilia. Its c and s look half unwrapped and its lowercase rivals the capitals, so a long page reads with generous, steady presence.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-newa: Stencilia is structural and striking, with a compact gap near the ascenders. Its strongest quality is the contrast with Noto Sans Newa, whose lowercase e has a clearly open mouth and generous bowls.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Stencilia is structural and striking, all stencil gaps and compact spacing. Noto Sans Ogham is the strongest quality here, its lowercase looking bold because the bodies stand so high, with wide gaps in the e.
